current_activity: debouches from Epinal toward Vittel; the Panther column bivouacs near Dompaire
notes: Event date: 12 September 1944, evening (Cole, ch. 4; Wikipedia). Event definition: On 12 September the brigade debouches from Epinal in two columns; the right column with the Panther battalion moves west toward Vittel and late in the day bivouacs near Dompaire, while the Mark IV column wheels south and then north (Cole, ch. 4; Wikipedia, Battle of Dompaire). Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). Cole, The Lorraine Campaign, ch. 4, p. 199: "Late in the day the right column of the 112th Panzer Brigade bivouacked near the village of Dompaire"; Wikipedia, Battle of Dompaire: "On the evening of 12 September, the German tanks had reached Dompaire". Location: Dompaire, Vosges with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Cole and Wikipedia name Dompaire. Commander: Colonel Horst von Usedom (Wikipedia, Battle of Dompaire).

current_activity: Panther column is destroyed around Dompaire by the French CCL and US fighter-bombers
notes: Event date: 13 September 1944 (Cole, ch. 4; Wikipedia). Event definition: On 13 September the French CCL (2nd Armored Division) and fighter-bombers drive the Panthers into a killing ground in the valley at Dompaire; in the afternoon seven Mark IVs of the south column are destroyed near Ville-sur-Illon; the brigade becomes little more than a cipher (Cole, ch. 4; Wikipedia, Battle of Dompaire). Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). Cole, The Lorraine Campaign, ch. 4, p. 195: "committed the 112th Panzer Brigade against the XV Corps, with such disastrous results as to make that panzer brigade little more than a cipher in future operational plans"; Wikipedia, Battle of Dompaire: "The inexperienced 112 Panzer Brigade suffered from a series of ambushes by French armoured units with American air support". Location: Dompaire, Vosges with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Cole and Wikipedia name Dompaire. Commander: Colonel Horst von Usedom (Wikipedia, Battle of Dompaire). Opponents: French 2nd Armored Division (Groupement Langlade, CCL); US 406th Fighter-Bomber Group.

current_activity: with the 21st Panzer Division, pulled back behind the Meurthe; detachments cut off by the French raid to Vathiménil
notes: Event date: night of 19-20 September 1944 (Cole, ch. 4). Event definition: After the 79th Division breaches the Mortagne line on 19 September, the 21st Panzer Division, reinforced by the brigade, is pulled back behind the Meurthe; detachments on the south flank are trapped by the French raid to Vathiménil and flee on foot, abandoning over two hundred vehicles and some tanks of the brigade (Cole, ch. 4). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Cole, The Lorraine Campaign, ch. 4, p. 207: "which had been reinforced by the 112th Panzer Brigade, back behind the Meurthe"; Cole, The Lorraine Campaign, ch. 4, p. 207: "abandoning over two hundred vehicles and some of the tanks belonging to the unfortunate 112th Panzer Brigade". Location: Vathiménil, Meurthe-et-Moselle (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Cole names Vathiménil. Commander: Colonel Horst von Usedom (Wikipedia, Battle of Dompaire). Opponents: US 79th Infantry Division; French 2nd Armored Division.

current_activity: brigade headquarters is chased out of Domjevin by a French patrol; one Panther and six Mark IVs left
notes: Event date: 23 September 1944 (Cole, ch. 5). Event definition: After the Dompaire debacle the brigade is down to one Panther and six Mark IVs and moving on foot; on 23 September a French patrol crosses La Vezouse and chases its headquarters out of Domjevin (Cole, ch. 5); a decree of 23 September dissolves it into the 21st Panzer Division (Wikipedia). Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). Cole, The Lorraine Campaign, ch. 5, p. 235: "chased the headquarters of the 112th Panzer Brigade out of Domjevin"; Cole, The Lorraine Campaign, ch. 5, p. 234: "had been reduced to one Panther and six Mark IV's"; Wikipedia, List of German brigades in World War II: "Dissolved as per a decree of 23 September 1944 and integrated into 21st Panzer Division". Location: Domjevin, Meurthe-et-Moselle (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Cole names Domjevin. Commander: Colonel Horst von Usedom (Wikipedia, Battle of Dompaire). Opponents: French 2nd Armored Division.
